title: Consumer Backlog: One Poison Event Blocks Fulfillment
businessContext: Fulfillment consumes six Kafka partitions. A new producer emits schema v3 while one consumer still expects v2. Partition 2 repeatedly fails on offset 8841, delaying every later order on that partition.
problemStatement: The oldest unfulfilled order is 24 minutes old; adding consumer replicas does not move partition 2. Work through three timed developments, justify your actions, and write an evidence-based incident response. The simulation starts paused; advancing time can expire unanswered decisions.
constraints: Preserve an auditable disposition for every order event.
Do not reset offsets to latest or silently discard failed records.
Kafka offsets and external fulfillment side effects need separate integrity controls.
All telemetry is synthetic. Actions only affect this practice simulation.
candidateTasks: Contain customer impact while preserving evidence and data integrity.
Respond to each new development and explain the selected action.
Cite telemetry supporting the root cause; distinguish observation from inference.
Define a permanent correction, regression coverage, recovery gates, and stakeholder update.

review.reasoning: Exactly-once claims must stop at the actual transactional boundary. Protect external side effects with durable business IDs and reconcile ranges, quarantine counts and order outcomes.

hints: All errors point to partition 2 offset 8841 with schema v3.
Stop or roll back incompatible production where safe and preserve the failed record plus its schema and coordinates.
Introduce schema compatibility checks and tolerant versioned consumers before producers switch.
alternativeApproaches: Use Kafka transactions for Kafka-to-Kafka transformations with read_committed consumers; external side effects remain a separate boundary.
Keep strict partition ordering and stop the partition until manual repair when skipping a record would violate domain invariants.
commonMistakes: Claiming Kafka exactly-once automatically prevents duplicate external shipments.
